acts.title: The Empty Valley
acts.blurb: Lay your first tiles: roads, towns, fields and priories.

acts.title: River and Market
acts.blurb: The valley grows rich. Rivals arrive with taverns, goods and masons.

acts.title: The Sable Claim
acts.blurb: A baron says the valley is his. Out-build his best settlers.

twists.how: Right after newGame, the boss seat's score starts at N instead of 0 (logged as 'starts with N points from old deeds').
Right after newGame, the boss seat's sup.f and figTotal.f are raised by N, so the boss has 7+N followers.
Right after newGame, the player's seat sup.f and figTotal.f are lowered by N, so the player has 7-N followers.
Right after newGame, the last N tiles of G.stack are removed and G.total is lowered by N, so the game ends N tiles sooner.
newGame is called with seats ['ai','human'] so the boss takes the first turn; metrics read the seat where human is true.
In complete(), each time a finished town pays the boss seat, the boss also gets N extra points, logged as 'town tithe +N'.

intro.text: Welcome to Vinemoor, Garnet. The valley is empty and the deeds go to whoever builds best.
Draw a tile, lay it so the edges match, then stand a follower on a road to claim it.
I'm Hob. I just haul carts about. Don't mind me!

outro.text: Every finished road paid you a point per tile, and your follower came home to work again.
Fair's fair. Your roads were straighter than mine.

opponent.name: Hob the Carter
opponent.personality: Friendly and careless; lays tiles almost at random.

easier.text: Hob already plays gently; follow the suggested move each turn.

intro.text: Towns pay best. A finished town gives 2 per tile and 2 per banner.
I'm Wren. I build walls for a living, so don't expect to out-build me.
Put a warden in a small town and close it fast. A 2-tile town is 4 points.

outro.text: Small towns closed quickly bring your wardens home for the next one.
Hm. You wall faster than I do.

opponent.name: Wren Ashlar
opponent.personality: Proud mason's apprentice who loves towns but leaves them unfinished.

goal.text: Win with at least 16 points from towns.

easier.text: Win with any number of town points.

intro.text: Farmers lie down in a field and never get up. Seems lazy, but it pays.
At the end, each field pays 3 points for every finished town it touches.
Lay one farmer early in a big field next to towns that will close.

outro.text: Told you. The lazy ones get fat on bread.
Fields are the quiet points. Many games are won in the last count.

opponent.name: Mabry Furrow
opponent.personality: Slow-talking farmer; happy to share a field rather than fight for it.

goal.text: Win with at least 9 points from fields.

easier.text: No river, and any field score will do: just win.

intro.text: Peace, settler. The priories of this valley were promised to my order.
A priory surrounded by 8 tiles is worth 9. Unfinished, it pays 1 per tile around it.
Quill builds priories and nothing else. Use everything you have learned.

outro.text: Your roads, towns, fields and priories... the valley speaks for you.
Word travels downriver. Merchants will come now, and harder rivals.

opponent.name: Brother Quill
opponent.personality: Calm and patient; sits brothers in priories and waits.
opponent.taunt: Patience is a virtue, settler. You lacked it today.
opponent.praise: Well built. I will write your name in the valley book.

easier.text: Just win; any score will do.

intro.text: Ferro, boatman. The river is mine to cross, and I know every bend.
The river tiles come first. They split fields, so plan your farmers around them.
Ferro plays properly now: he finishes what he starts. Watch his followers.

outro.text: You crossed well. Keep the ferry fee, you earned it.

opponent.name: Ferro the Boatman
opponent.personality: Steady and practical; takes the best points on offer each turn.

intro.text: Dulcie Tapwell. My taverns double a road, and my basilicas triple a town.
Careful: a road with a tavern or a town with a basilica pays nothing if unfinished.
You also get a champion. It counts as two followers when deciding who owns a feature.

outro.text: A round on the house. You closed what you opened.

opponent.name: Dulcie Tapwell
opponent.personality: Bold gambler; loves big basilica towns and moves in on yours with her champion.

easier.text: Dulcie plays gently and any winning score counts.

intro.text: I am Reeve Ostrand. Every barrel of wine in this valley is taxed by me.
Whoever closes a town takes its goods. The most wine, grain or cloth is worth 10 each.
Your mason gives an extra turn when you grow its feature; your hog fattens a field.
And as reeve, I move first. Market rules.

outro.text: The ledger does not lie. The market is yours, settler.
But a darker banner flies on the north ridge. Sable.

opponent.name: Reeve Ostrand
opponent.personality: Cold bookkeeper; closes towns for their goods even when they score him little.
opponent.taunt: Paid in full. Better luck at the next market.
opponent.praise: Your accounts balance better than mine. Well traded.

twist.text: Boss rule: Reeve Ostrand takes the first turn.

easier.text: You move first and the Reeve plays gently.

intro.text: Isolde, of Lilac Hall. The Baron sent me to see if you are worth a fight.
She plays the best game you have faced: she counts the tiles still in the bag.
No tricks this time. Just the base valley, and the river.

outro.text: I'll tell the Baron you are worth a fight. He won't like it.

opponent.name: Isolde of Lilac Hall
opponent.personality: Polite and exact; never wastes a follower and blocks your towns from closing.

easier.text: Isolde plays at the normal level.

intro.text: Corvin Blackmere, the Baron's steward. I bring an extra pair of hands.
He has 8 followers to your 7. Spend yours carefully and bring them home often.

outro.text: Eight hands, and still you out-built me. The Baron will come himself.

opponent.name: Corvin Blackmere
opponent.personality: Sly and grasping; floods the board with followers and steals shared fields.

twist.text: Boss rule: Corvin starts with 8 followers instead of 7.

easier.text: Corvin plays at the normal level with 7 followers.

intro.text: This valley was my grandfather's. I hold old deeds worth 15 points before we begin.
All three expansions, his best play, and a head start. This is the last deed.
Close towns, guard your fields, and count the tiles left. You know how.

outro.text: The old deeds are ash. Vinemoor is yours.
Garnet of Vinemoor. It has a ring to it.
Told everyone you'd do it. Mostly.

opponent.name: The Sable Baron
opponent.personality: Arrogant and ruthless; contests every big town and farms the whole valley.
opponent.taunt: Old deeds always win. Go back to your carts.
opponent.praise: I yield. Keep the valley, and my banner with it.

twist.text: Boss rule: the Sable Baron starts with 15 points.

goal.text: Win the game against the Baron's 15-point head start.

easier.text: The Baron plays at the normal level with no head start.
